fix_tasks.title: Tearing and stair-steps at in-between cameras (pop, release, intro, pointer easing): continuous projector visibility and a fill blur that does not depend on camera distance
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: Hold-sweep MAJOR (+1.0). In sw_pop_B, sw_pop_BL and sw_pop_TR the floe edges are torn into 1-2 px hairlines and dashes about 140 px long (x500-643, y657-670). sw_rel_BL shows a staircase of white blocks (x32-62, y522-568) and a comb of ticks (x1100-1150, y636-644). sw_tau_0.25 (camera x 0.48) has a 32x8 px striped rock smear at the frame bottom (x586-618, y739-747); the same spot is clean at camera x 0.23. sw_intro_0 has a torn tab and a dotted ghost outline (x305-350, y718-760). Hold-sweep minor (+0.35): the reflection columns are stair-stepped (sw_pop_B x966-1000, sw_hold_R x1330-1363), and a small floe is clipped by a vertical edge (x≈1146).
fix_tasks.root_cause:
(a)

Visible() in occlusionGLSL takes 5 binary step() taps on a NearestFilter, 1536-wide RGBA16F depth map. Each extra projector's weight (u

Mix*visK*inK) therefore jumps in steps of 0.2 on the depth-texel grid, which is 2-3 px during the dolly. Neighbouring pixels flip between plates baked from different viewpoints. (b) PLATE_FRAG blurs filled fragments only by smoothstep(1.0, 4.0, distance(cameraPosition, uPlateCamPos)). Within about 1 m of the rest projector (the pointer easing back, the start of the intro), the per-row sideways fill from plateUnoccluded is sampled crisp, which produces the striped smears. (c) WATER_FRAG blurs the lake fill only where 'raised' (lod = lodX + 3*raised); every other moved lookup stays crisp. (d) The mirror distance (.b) used to be read with a nearest lookup. That part is now handled: mirrorLGLSL (an edge-aware, 2x2-filtered L) landed in Water.ts at 12:17.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan: 1) Rewrite Visible() as a bilinear PCF. Set st = uv/texel - 0.5, base = (floor(st)+0.5)*texel, f = fract(st). Take four taps at base + {0,1}²·texel, each v = smoothstep(lim-0.4, lim+0.4, depth*1.06) with lim = fz-0.8, and mix them bilinearly. That is 4 taps instead of 5, so ANGLE compile memory does not grow. Only if edges still read hard, use 2×4 taps at ±0.75 texel on T1+. 2) In PLATE_FRAG set filled = moved * smoothstep(0.02, 0.3, camAway), so the blur is zero only at the projector itself. 3) In WATER_FRAG set lod = lodX + 3.0*max(raised, step(1e-5, distance(puv, puv0)) * smoothstep(0.02, 0.3, camAway)). 4) Verify that the landed mirrorL filter cleans the reflection columns. 5) Re-run shoot_sweep. Only if the pop or release still tears, add dolly-path projectors 'pop' (r≈14.7 m) and 'rel' (r≈17.6 m) in the T24 bake. Compare against F358, F420 and F453, which show unbroken slabs.
fix_tasks.expected_gain: glitch_hold_sweep +1.0 to +1.3, glitch_cursor_orbit +0.1, environment +0.05. Overall ≈ +0.01; this is a red-line fix (tearing).
fix_tasks.risk: Medium. Softer visibility can bleed a projector's anti-aliased rim onto the sky or lake behind a silhouette (the iceberg rim, the ridge crest at hold_TR and pop_TR). The Rim re-projection stays, and the ±0.4 m band is tight. More blur in fills can read as soft smudges near rocks at small pointer offsets. fix_tasks.root_cause: Pop: Choreography starts B's split at tp 0.65 (EXPAND_POP). disagreements:
1) Rest massif. The environment judge says it matches: x300-420, y260-340 reads 160,173,192 vs 159,174,194. The grade judge says the upper massif is 20-35 levels too bright at x230-330, y220-300. These are different boxes: the main face matches, but the shoulder under the summit and its wisp does not. Call: no global change to the massif at rest. T08 darkens it only in the hold. Re-measure the shoulder box after T14, and treat it as a local summit-wisp fix if it stays more than +15 levels bright.
2) Near floes in the hold. The hold-sweep judge wants crisp slabs ('F420 crisp, flat slabs'). The environment judge wants softer, hazier floes without inked edges. In zoom z21 (F420 at the bottom, p06 at the top), F420's floes are pale and low-contrast but not smeared. Call: remove the hold near-field blur (T04) and lift the dark undercuts toward the fog (T08). That gives crisp shapes with hazy values, which satisfies both.
3) The hold fog. The awwwards and hold-sweep judges praise the soft, graded hold fog. The environment and grade judges measure it as too thin, too blue and too flat against F420 (sd 7.1 vs 23.6; B-R 48 vs 37). Call: the measurements win. Make it denser, more neutral and billowy (T08), but keep the soft top edge that the glitch judge praised.
4) Ice brightness. The ice and awwwards judges say exposure matches (194 vs 200) and must not be darkened. The grade judge says the pop/hold hero is too bright and white (pop centre L212.7 vs 199.7). Call: leave rest exposure alone. The pop/hold excess comes from the ice's orb-light floor and the bloom, so fix those with energy/camExpand gates (T09). Add contrast to the ice through structure (T11), not through gain.
5) Orb exposure. The orb judge finds the exposed orb too hot at p05 and p07 (94 % clipped vs 60 %). The round-8 stats show the engine clipping less than the reference at q00 and q03 (28 vs 900 px; 1308 vs 2453), and the composition and awwwards judges call the hold orb dark. Call: this depends on the pose. Redistribute the light rather than change the gain: a smaller, smoky hot zone when the orb is fully exposed and a glowing cap in the hold (T07), plus clipping through the ice (T09).
6) Cause of the bottom band. The cursor-orbit judge assumes the plates carry only ~15 px of bottom overscan. The plates actually carry 0.13 (~100 px), and the low-pointer pan is ~27 px. Call: no re-bake for coverage. The band comes from the plate/lake grading seam plus z-fighting, which T01 fixes.
7) Glitches at the bottom. The awwwards judge says the pointer poses are glitch-free with nothing weird at the bottom. The cursor-orbit judge's zooms show the band in all three low-pointer poses. Call: the zoomed evidence wins, so T01 stays first.
8) Ripples. The awwwards judge wants rings 2-3x stronger and crisp. Round 7 judged round 6's stronger shading as painted stripes, and the water box sd now equals F000's (39.0 vs 38.8). Call: sharpen the crest shape, make the troughs bluer, widen the glint and remove the radial smear, but keep the amplitude and sd (T19).
9) Edges. The hold-sweep judge says the ring silhouettes are anti-aliased. The ice and awwwards judges report 1-px stepped edges and dashed rims. Call: both are right. The geometry is MSAA'd on T1, but the lines come from shader terms and the half-res refraction, which T18 fixes.
10) Release snap. The hold-sweep judge says the segmented release matches F453. The composition judge says the gaps are rotated about 45 deg and too narrow. Call: the layout is right; refine the gap phase and width at low priority (T20).
11) Shard density. The composition judge says the belt density matches at rest and in the hold. The orb judge measures half the coverage in the hold (1.12 % vs 2.10 %). Call: leave rest unchanged and scale the hold up modestly (T15).
12) Bloom and orb tint. The grade judge asks for a pale-cyan bloom ×(0.88,0.97,1.0), which leans blue. The orb judge asks for mint-cyan with G ≥ B. Call: mint-cyan with G ≥ B for the orb band and the limb (T07); the environment diffusion band stays neutral.
13) Ice silhouettes. The ice judge wants fewer high-frequency notches but praises the lumpy low-frequency outline, and earlier rounds called the rings 'perfect circles'. Call: keep the low-frequency lumps that #55 kept, and cut only the high-frequency crease and chips (T16).
14) The doubled far range. The environment judge calls it major and the hold-sweep judge calls it a minor 'cardboard matte'. The cursor-orbit judge saw no doubling in any pointer pose, although the environment judge found a faint ghost in ptr_left. Call: one root cause, already fixed in deploy #57; verify all of these spots (T02).
15) Code that moved during this review. The round-9 captures are of deploy #51. Since then, the code has picked up the q01 tips (#52), the hold orb rim zone (#53), the B lips (#54), smaller silhouette chips (#55), the shard facet cap (#56), the skyGate fix (#57), and, in the working tree, the water/overscan near-black lifts, the edge-aware mirror-L filter and a global cut to the bloom UP_WEIGHTS. Call: tasks T02, T06, T07, T09, T15 and T16 start by verifying what has landed before adding anything.
